questions.question:
Which of the following idiom given in the alternatives has the meaning?

Barely in time, at the last moment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Under the wire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Under the wire"** means accomplishing something barely in time or at the last possible moment. (किसी काम को अंतिम समय में पूरा करना)
 
 
• **Example:** She submitted her assignment under the wire, just minutes before the deadline.
 
 
• This idiom is often used in situations where there is a sense of urgency or pressure to complete something before a specified deadline.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Under the wire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Over the schedule** (समय सीमा से अधिक): Refers to exceeding the planned or allotted time for a task.
 
 
• **Example:** The construction project went over the schedule due to unexpected delays.
 
 
 
• **Under the minute hand** (मिनट की सुई के नीचे): This phrase is not a commonly recognized idiom in English and does not convey the intended meaning of completing something at the last moment.
 
 
• **Example:** This option does not apply to the context of the question.
 
 
 
• **Over the clock** (घड़ी के समय से अधिक): This phrase is also not a standard idiom in English and does not fit the meaning of completing something barely in time.
 
 
• **Example:** This option does not convey the correct meaning for the given question.

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

The unprecedented decrease of direct taxes has increased the earning potential of the capitalists.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the preposition "**of**" used after the noun "**decrease**."
 
• When referring to a reduction in the quantity, quality, or amount of something, the noun "**decrease**" (or "increase") is conventionally followed by the preposition "**in**."
 
• The phrase "**decrease in direct taxes**" is the standard idiomatic expression to describe a change within that category.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The unprecedented **decrease in direct taxes** has increased the earning potential of the capitalists."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The unprecedented"** – This is correct. "Unprecedented" is an adjective meaning never done or known before, and it correctly modifies the noun "decrease."
 
• **Option 3: "increased the earning"** – This part is grammatically correct; "increased" is the past participle used with "has" to form the present perfect tense.
 
• **Option 4: "potential of the capitalists."** – This is correct. "Potential of" is a standard way to show possession or relationship.
 
• **Prepositional Rule:** Words denoting a rise or fall (increase, decrease, rise, fall, drop, decline) usually take the preposition "**in**" when followed by the thing that is changing (e.g., "a fall **in** prices," "an increase **in** temperature").

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

There is an irreparable problem of the ignition system of the car, which has to be addressed immediately.

options.text: of the ignition system of the car,
which has to be addressed immediately.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the prepositional phrase "**problem of**" used to describe a mechanical or functional fault.
 
• In English, when referring to a malfunction, difficulty, or an issue related to a specific object or system, the preposition "**with**" is the standard idiomatic choice.
 
• The phrase "**problem with the ignition system**" correctly indicates that the fault exists within that specific part of the car.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"There is an irreparable **problem with the ignition system** of the car, which has to be addressed immediately."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "There is an"** – This part is correct. "An" is the appropriate indefinite article used before the vowel sound in "irreparable."
 
• **Option 2: "irreparable problem"** – This part is grammatically sound. "Irreparable" is an adjective modifying the noun "problem."
 
• **Option 4: "which has to be addressed immediately."** – This is correct. "Which" is a relative pronoun introducing a non-defining clause, and "addressed immediately" correctly uses the passive voice and an adverb.
 
• **'Problem of' vs 'Problem with':** We generally use "**problem of**" for broad, abstract, or societal issues (e.g., "the problem of unemployment") and "**problem with**" for specific things that are not working correctly (e.g., "a problem with the computer").

__

questions.question: How does the Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) differ from the traditional higher education system?

options.text: It allows students to pick courses based on their career goals.
It requires students to follow a fixed curriculum with no flexibility.
It limits students to a single discipline and discourages skill development.
It focuses solely on memorization and theoretical knowledge.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: It allows students to pick courses based on their career goals.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that CBCS **"empowers students with the autonomy to shape their academic journey according to their interests and aspirations."**
 
• Unlike the traditional system, it offers a **"diverse array of courses,"** including interdisciplinary and skill-based ones, providing **"flexibility and customization options"** that allow students to align their studies with their future career paths.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: It requires students to follow a fixed curriculum with no flexibility.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. This description applies to the **traditional education structures** mentioned in the text, which CBCS is designed to replace with a more "dynamic" and flexible framework.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It limits students to a single discipline and discourages skill development.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text highlights that CBCS specifically includes **"interdisciplinary and skill-based"** courses alongside core subjects.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: It focuses solely on memorization and theoretical knowledge.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. By including **"skill-based"** courses and focusing on "holistic development," the system moves away from a purely theoretical or rote-learning approach.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core, Elective, and Foundation**: Under CBCS, courses are usually categorized into **Core** (compulsory), **Elective** (chosen from a pool), and **Foundation** (value-based or skill-enhancement) papers.
 
• **NEP 2020**: The New Education Policy emphasizes the "multidisciplinary" nature of education, and CBCS is a primary vehicle to achieve this by breaking the silos between arts, sciences, and commerce.
 
• **UGC (University Grants Commission)**: This is the statutory body in India responsible for maintaining standards of higher education. The passage notes that CBCS is a pivotal tool recommended by the UGC.

questions.question: How does CBCS fit into the vision of the New Education Policy (NEP)?

options.text: It goes against NEP by sticking to rigid subject structures and limiting student choice
It ignores NEP recommendations and continues with outdated, one-size-fits-all curricula and discourages learners from thinking out of the box
It slows down NEP implementation by resisting reforms and discouraging skill-based education for the learners
It supports NEP reforms by encouraging flexibility, interdisciplinary learning, and global alignment in higher education

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: It supports NEP reforms by encouraging flexibility, interdisciplinary learning, and global alignment in higher education.***

 
 
• The passage identifies CBCS as a **"pivotal tool"** for the reforms currently happening under the **New Education Policy (NEP)**.
 
• It aligns with the NEP vision by offering **"flexibility and customization,"** enabling **"interdisciplinary"** study, and ensuring that the Indian system is **"inspired by international educational models"** to reach global standards.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: It goes against NEP by sticking to rigid subject structures...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text describes CBCS as the opposite of rigid; it is a **"dynamic framework"** that provides students with the **"autonomy"** to choose their courses.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: It ignores NEP recommendations and continues with outdated curricula...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage explicitly states that CBCS is **"recommended by the UGC"** specifically to align with the reforms of the NEP.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It slows down NEP implementation by resisting reforms...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Rather than resisting, CBCS is described as **"revolutionizing the landscape"** and serving as a key instrument in executing the NEP's goals.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NEP 2020 Vision**: The policy aims to transform India into a "global knowledge superpower" by making education more holistic, flexible, and multidisciplinary. CBCS is the structural mechanism that allows this flexibility.
 
• **Interdisciplinary Learning**: This allows a student of Science to take a course in Music or Economics, breaking the traditional "silos" of education that the NEP seeks to remove.
 
• **Global Standards**: By using a credit-based system, Indian degrees become more easily comparable to those from international universities, facilitating student mobility and global recognition.

questions.question: Which educational philosophy influenced the adoption of CBCS in India?

options.text: Traditional Indian models emphasizing rote learning
Government schemes focused solely on vocational training
International frameworks advocating flexibility and learner autonomy
Systems designed to reduce academic diversity and specialization

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: International frameworks advocating flexibility and learner autonomy.***

 
 
• The passage clearly states that CBCS is **"Inspired by international educational models."**
 
• It further elaborates that these models focus on **"autonomy"** for the student, allowing them to **"shape their academic journey"** based on individual interests.
 
• This philosophy shifts the focus from a rigid, one-size-fits-all approach to one characterized by **"flexibility and customization,"** which are core tenets of modern international educational frameworks.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Traditional Indian models emphasizing rote learning.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text positions CBCS as a departure from **"traditional education structures,"** aiming for "holistic development" rather than the memorization associated with rote learning.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Government schemes focused solely on vocational training.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While CBCS includes **"skill-based"** courses, it integrates them **"alongside core subjects"** within a broader academic framework, rather than focusing *solely* on vocational training.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Systems designed to reduce academic diversity...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. CBCS is designed to **increase** diversity by offering a **"diverse array of courses"** and **"interdisciplinary"** options.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Learner Autonomy**: This is a philosophy where the student takes responsibility for their own learning. In CBCS, this is manifested through the ability to choose electives and "soft" subjects that align with personal career goals.
 
• **Holistic Education**: The "holistic development" mentioned in the text refers to an educational philosophy that seeks to develop all aspects of the learner—intellectual, emotional, social, and physical—rather than just academic knowledge.
 
• **Global Comparability**: By adopting international philosophies of flexibility and credit-based weights, Indian degrees become more "portable," making it easier for students to seek employment or further education in global markets.
